memory_update.text: Core direct candidates for dispatchable power capacity are CEG, VST, TLN, NRG, PEG, DUK, SO, ETR, and D because they own or procure nuclear/gas firm generation assets.

Core supply-chain bottleneck candidates are GEV for gas turbines/services, BWXT for specialized nuclear components, CCJ for uranium/Westinghouse reactor-services exposure, and LEU for enrichment/HALEU.

The node should be tracked across two parallel mechanisms: scarcity value of existing dispatchable assets and physical supply constraints for new reliable capacity, especially gas turbine delivery slots and nuclear fuel/component constraints.
Need deeper verification of ISO-level exposure, capacity-market revenues, hedging, contract duration, gas fuel access, and regulatory treatment before ranking candidates.

Gas turbine supply chain has fewer US-listed pure plays than the asset-owner side; non-US OEMs and private suppliers may be important but are outside or only indirectly accessible through US listings.

node: Dispatchable generation: gas turbines, nuclear plants, capacity markets, reliability resources
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around dispatchable power capacity. The strongest direct mappings are existing nuclear and gas fleet owners exposed to scarcity pricing, capacity markets, bilateral power deals, and reliability needs; gas turbine OEM/service exposure; and nuclear fuel/components/EPC suppliers that enable or constrain new reliable capacity. This is research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell list.
